name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
principle: The product constructs an OS command using externally influenced input without correctly neutralizing command-control characters or separating data from code. Attackers can change the command executed by the OS and run commands with the product's privileges.
detection_signals: C/C++ system(cmd) where cmd contains argv, getenv(), request, socket, file, or config input
C/C++ popen(cmd, mode) where cmd is built by strcat, sprintf, snprintf, std::string +, or ostringstream with external input
C/C++ execl("/bin/sh", "sh", "-c", cmd, NULL) or execv shell with -c and external input
Java Runtime.getRuntime().exec(String) where the string contains concatenated external input
Java ProcessBuilder("sh", "-c", cmd) or ProcessBuilder("cmd.exe", "/C", cmd) with external input
command string concatenates input near shell metacharacters: ;, &, &&, |, ||, `, $(), >, <, newline
program name or executable path comes from request parameter, environment variable, system property, or attacker-writable config
negative_signals: C/C++ execve(fixedAbsolutePath, argvArray, envp) with user input only as one argv element
Java new ProcessBuilder(fixedProgram, userArg).start() without sh -c or cmd.exe /C
external input is checked by strict allowlist regex before command use, e.g. ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$
code uses a library API instead of an OS command, e.g. InetAddress.getByName(host) instead of nslookup
executable path and command are constants and no external input reaches command construction
false_defense_traps: denylist removes only ';' but leaves &, &&, |, ||, `, $(), >, <, or newline
HTML, XML, URL, or SQL encoding is applied before shell execution
quoting the whole command string while allowing embedded quotes or command substitution
Runtime.exec(String) is assumed safe while the string invokes sh -c or cmd.exe /C
shell metacharacters are blocked but untrusted input can still inject options or arguments, causing CWE-88
verification_focus: Can attacker-controlled data select or modify an OS command without strict allowlisting or fixed argv-array separation?

consequence_chains.trigger: external input is concatenated into an OS command string
incomplete denylist misses a shell separator or command substitution syntax
injected command runs in a privileged process
consequence_chains.consequence: privileged file access or privilege escalation

consequence_chains.trigger: shell is avoided but untrusted input remains an unconstrained argv option
consequence_chains.consequence: argument or option injection into the invoked program

patch_principle: Replace OS commands with library calls when possible.
Avoid shell invocation; use fixed executable paths and argv-array APIs.
Validate each argument with a strict allowlist for length, charset, and business rules.
If shell use is unavoidable, quote and escape each argument for the exact target shell.
Run invoked processes with least privilege and sandboxing to limit impact.
